The Centurion's Servant
sen-TYOOR-ee-un
noun phrase
From the Latin centurio, a Roman officer over a hundred men, whose servant Christ healed at a word for the master’s great faith.

📖 Biblical Definition

There came unto Christ a centurion, beseeching Him, and saying, Lord, my servant lieth at home sick of the palsy, grievously tormented. And Jesus saith unto him, I will come and heal him (Mat 8:6; Mat 8:7). But the centurion answered, Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldest come under my roof: but speak the word only, and my servant shall be healed (Mat 8:8). For he was a man set under authority; and he reasoned that as his own word commanded men, so the word of Christ commanded sickness and health, needing no journey but a word alone. When Jesus heard it, He marvelled, and said to them that followed, Verily I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel (Mat 8:10). And He said unto the centurion, Go thy way; and as thou hast believed, so be it done unto thee. And his servant was healed in the selfsame hour (Mat 8:13). The dictionary marks this healing as the great example of faith that rests on the bare word of Christ. The man was a Gentile and a soldier, yet his faith outran that of Israel, and Christ used it to foretell that many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham in the kingdom of heaven (Mat 8:11). So the Scripture teaches the sufficiency of Christ’s word, and that true faith honours Him by trusting His word though He be not seen.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A Roman centurion’s servant, healed at a word for the master’s faith, which Christ said surpassed Israel’s.

📖 Key Scripture

Mat 8:8 — "The centurion answered and said, Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldest come under my roof: but speak the word only, and my servant shall be healed."

Mat 8:10 — "When Jesus heard it, he marvelled, and said to them that followed, Verily I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel."

Mat 8:13 — "And Jesus said unto the centurion, Go thy way; and as thou hast believed, so be it done unto thee. And his servant was healed in the selfsame hour."

Mat 8:11 — "And I say unto you, That many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A miracle of Christ; the healing shews great faith resting on the bare word of Christ, who heals though unseen.

expand to see more

The healing of the centurion’s servant has drawn little redefinition from the present age, surviving as the great Gospel example of faith that Christ Himself commended. The dictionary records it that the reader may mark the power of Christ to heal at a distance by a word, and the faith of a Gentile soldier that surpassed Israel’s.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is faith that rests upon the bare word of Christ. The centurion asked no touch and no nearness, but the word only, reasoning that as his own word commanded men, so the word of Christ commanded sickness; and Christ marvelled and called it the greatest faith in Israel. So the dictionary draws the sign: that Christ’s word is sufficient and almighty, healing though He be not seen, and that the inclusion of this Gentile in such faith foretold the gathering of many from the east and west to sit down in the kingdom of heaven, by faith in the same word.
